findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done - For a repo whose test setting runs one combined script with no quick-test setting, the setup check, upgrade and adoption each print one line saying so and suggest no command, and the shipped guide explains how the agent writes the quicker command.
Case: normal use - a repo running Forge v1.2.38 upgrades with Forge's generated Node test setting and a `test` script such as `tsc && vitest run && playwright test`.
The v1.2.38 `src/forge/upgrade.py:201` calls its own `quicktest.suggest` before installing and running the new release's sync. Its `quicktest.py:59-67,102-115` prints an npm quick-test suggestion whose Vitest flags reach Playwright. The guard here runs only in the new release, so the later advisory from `src/forge/sync.py:743` cannot suppress that incorrect suggestion. The upgrade proof still starts this checkout's Forge (`tests/test_upgrade_command.py:87-88`, `tests/conftest.py:59-69`) and uses a script without a direct Vitest invocation (`tests/test_combined_script_quick_test.py:21,76`), so it misses the failure.
findings.title: Not done: Upgrades started by an older Forge use the old suggestion logic

why: Today, when a repo's test setting runs one combined script and has no quick-test setting, Forge prints a wrong suggested command for some such repos, prints nothing for others, and prints nothing at all when it adopts a live app.
